name: stack-trace
title: Stack trace
description: An error's stack trace made readable: your own frames in full weight, library frames folded away, copyable file locations and one button for the whole trace.
docs: Pass an error ({ name, message, stack }) and the stack is parsed into frames (V8's 'at fn (file:1:2)' and the 'fn@file:1:2' of Firefox and Safari), or pass frames you parsed yourself. Frames in node_modules, in Node's own modules, in native code or outside projectRoot are library code: runs of them fold under 'Show 8 library frames' with the packages they come from, or are open from the start with defaultExpanded. Your own frames show the function in full weight with the file location under it, relative to projectRoot, and the first one is set apart as 'Start here'. Every file location is a button that copies 'src/cart.tsx:42:13' (its copy glyph shows on hover and focus, and always on a touch screen, and a long path wraps after a slash and not in the middle of a file name), and Copy trace copies the whole trace as plain text, the original stack when you gave one. The frames are an ordered list under a heading, and copies are announced politely (onCopied is called with the text); a clipboard that refuses is said on the card too, in words, not only to a screen reader. parseStack and the other helpers are in stack-trace/parse for servers and tests.
